chunks.arabic_text: ٣١ - مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ بِشِيرٍ، الْبَرْمَكِيُّ، أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ، الْمَعْرُوفُ بِصَاحِبِ الصُّومَعَةِ. ضَعِيفٌ.

translations.en: 31 – Muḥammad b. Ismāʿīl b. Aḥmad b. Bashīr, al-Barmakī, Abū Jaʿfar, the one who is known as the possessor of the hermitage. Weak.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri's *Kitab al-Duafa* identifies Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl as 'al-Barmakī,' a nisba likely referencing his lineage or association with the prominent Barmakid family, a key political and scholarly dynasty in the Abbasid era. The classification of 'weak' (ḍaʿīf) indicates that while he was a recognized narrator, his hadiths are not considered definitive proof in Shia jurisprudence due to minor deficiencies in memory or precision. This reflects the rigorous scrutiny applied to narrators to ensure the authenticity of the Imams' teachings.
en.seo_question: Who is Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl al-Barmakī and what is his status as a hadith narrator?

key_terms.صَاحِبِ الصُّومَعَةِ: Possessor of the hermitage (a title indicating a specific residence or status)
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak (a technical term in hadith sciences indicating a narrator with less than perfect reliability)
key_terms.الْبَرْمَكِيُّ: Al-Barmakī (a nisba indicating origin or association with the Barmakid family or region)
